findings.title: /users total_count is 0 past the last page
findings.problem: get_users_money_page derives total_count as the max over the returned page rows. A page index past the end (or per_page=0) returns no rows, so total_count is 0. The story requires counts to match the baseline exactly, and the old handler returned the full developer count regardless of page.
findings.impact: Response-contract change on GET /users?page=N. A pagination UI reading total_count on an out-of-range page sees an empty dataset. Fails AC6 (counts exact), a required criterion.
findings.recommendation: Compute the distinct developer count from sel in a scalar subquery or separate column that is outside LIMIT/OFFSET, and read total_count from that.
findings.check_notes: reader.py users page: total_count from count(DISTINCT developer) FROM sel, outside page; test asserts beyond.total_count == 4

fix.change: total_count is now a scalar count of distinct developers in sel, outside LIMIT/OFFSET

findings.title: Stored-groups cap counts the whole table, not the window
findings.problem: model_groups_mode reads S from session_dims for the whole table (rates_version IS NULL OR model_groups_rev differs) with a hard-coded GROUPS_S_CAP of 1000. It includes never-valid sessions and in-flight unstamped ones, and the reader never passes s_cap. The guide says the cap applies to sessions of the window and to the configured s_cap.
findings.impact: Over 1000 permanently never-valid or in-flight sessions push every dashboard request to the all-live form, which the bench puts at 22 s or more against a 30 s statement limit. The only signal is a rate-limited WARNING. Reachability of the sustained-over-cap state was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Exclude never-valid rows from S, scope S to the request's sel before applying the cap, and pass the configured cap from the reader. If the table-wide design is intended, update the guide.
findings.check_notes: reader passes self._s_cap to model_groups_mode; S from pending index, cap configurable (default 5000); guide updated to match

fix.change: reader passes its configured s_cap to model_groups_mode; guide states S is table-wide with that cap

findings.title: No route-level 504 test for /cost, /users, /user-charts
findings.problem: Only a synthetic endpoint is tested for the timeout_504 mapping. Dropping timeout_504 on any of the three dashboard routes keeps every test green.
findings.impact: The request budget and the dashboard-slot wait raise TimeoutError. Without the opt-in the route answers 503 instead of 504, which breaks AC9.
findings.recommendation: Add route tests that make the handler raise TimeoutError and asyncpg.QueryCanceledError for each route, and assert status 504 and the _ERR_DASHBOARD_TIMEOUT message.
findings.check_notes: routes carry timeout_504; parametrized tests assert 504 and _ERR_DASHBOARD_TIMEOUT for QueryCanceledError and TimeoutError on all three

fix.change: route-level tests for /cost, /users, /user-charts mapping QueryCanceledError and TimeoutError to 504
